Luminous

LOO-muh-nus -- shares a root with 'illuminate,' meaning light. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Luminous is full of light, or glowing with light of its own.

Deep in the cave, tiny luminous organisms lit the ceiling like a scattering of stars.

Worked Example

On a moonless night at sea, the water itself seems to glow every time a wave breaks, lit from within by countless microscopic creatures.

That quality of giving off or being filled with light is exactly what luminous describes. Unlike 'dim,' which suggests weak light, luminous means bright enough to notice immediately.

How Luminous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

radiant

radiant: sending out light brightly

glowing

glowing: giving off a steady light

incandescent

incandescent: glowing white-hot from intense heat, like a lamp filament; luminous is broader - anything filled with light or shining with its own light

Antonyms

murky

murky: dark and gloomy

dim

dim: not bright; giving little light

How Strong Is It? — glowing → luminous → radiant

glowing vs. luminous

glowing vs. luminous: Glowing is a bit softer than luminous -- glowing often suggests a gentle, steady light, while luminous can describe something bright enough to be genuinely striking in the dark.

radiant vs. luminous

radiant vs. luminous: Radiant can feel even brighter than luminous: luminous simply means giving off light, while radiant suggests that light seems to spread outward with real warmth or energy.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — -lumin-/-lum-

root — -lumin-/-lum-: light (Latin (lumen, luminis))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin lumen meant 'light.' Luminous, at its root, describes something filled with or giving off light -- the same root that gives us illuminate and luminary.

Use the root in a new word: illuminate

Use the root in a new word: illuminate: A single lantern was enough to illuminate the entire cabin during the blackout.

Word Choice

Luminous can describe something that literally glows, like a luminous dial, or something figuratively radiant, like luminous prose.
